newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen blames abductions on foreign-backed saboteurs.
newsitem.headline: Yemen blames abductions on foreign-backed saboteurs.

text.p: Yemen has blamed foreign-backed saboteurs for a spate of kidnappings of foreigners it said were aimed at harming the international relations of the poor Arab state.
The charge was made in a statement issued by an official security source and published in Yemeni newspapers on Sunday.
"Foreign-backed saboteurs are tragetting nationals of countries with whom we have friendly relations and strong economic ties," the statement said. It did not name the alleged foreign powers.
Yemeni officials had previously alleged foreign backing to the kidnappers. Some had blamed the abductions on Yemeni opposition groups receiving Saudi financial help.

Yemen on Friday secured the release of 10 Italian tourists kidnapped by tribesmen in separate incidents last week, the latest in a spate of abductions in recent years that targetted European tourists, Western diplomats and a Saudi ambassador.
The tribesmen have tried to use hostages as bargaining chips in disputes with the government and foreign oil firms. All hostages have so far been released unharmed.
Cash-strapped Yemen is rich in archeological sites which attract scores of tourists mainly from Europe. It put its 1996 revenue from its emerging tourism sector at $50 million.
Yemen, a small independent oil producer, depends heavily on foreign aid mainly from Europe and other Western donors.
